title: PLEASE TAKE NOTICE OF PLANNING COMMISSION PUBLIC HEARING NOVEMBER 18, 2026 AT 6:30 PM
text: AUGUSTA CHARTER TOWNSHIP NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING PLANNING COMMISSION Notice is hereby given that the Augusta Charter Township Planning Commission will hold a Public Hearing on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at 6:30 p.m. at the Lincoln Senior Center, 8970 Whittaker Road (west entrance of Brick Elementary), Ypsilanti, MI 48197. The purpose of this public hearing is to receive public input and to consider a proposed amendment to the Augusta Charter Township Zoning Ordinance. The proposed amendment would establish a six (6) month temporary moratorium on certain zoning approvals and applications related to High Resource Demand Facilities, including data centers, while the Township reviews and develops zoning regulations addressing these facilities and their potential impacts on infrastructure, utilities, surrounding land uses, and public health, safety, and welfare. If you have any written comments or concerns, they can be sent to the Augusta Charter Township Planning Commission, P.O. Box 100, Whittaker, MI 48190-0100 or by email to the Township Clerk – clerk@augustatownship.org and should be received prior to 4:00 PM on November 18, 2026. A copy of the proposed ordinance amendment is available for public inspection at the Augusta Charter Township offices during regular business hours located at 8021 Talladay Rd, Willis, MI 48191. Augusta Township Planning Commission PUBLISH: November 1, 2026

title: November 10, 2026
text: East China Charter Township Official Board Minutes November 10, 2025 EAST CHINA CHARTER TOWNSHIP OFFICIAL PROCEEDINGS NOVEMBER 10, 2025 CALL TO ORDER – Supervisor Westrick called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., with Clerk Smith, Treasurer Horn, and Trustees Kline, Babel, Reichle & Biebuyck. Also present: Director of Public Services, Dwayne Loper and Koryn Garwood, Bookkeeper. Thirty-five in the audience. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE APPROVE AGENDA – Clerk Smith, supported by Treasurer Horn, moved to approve the Agenda. Carried. PUBLIC HEARING FOR 2026 BUDGETS Trustee Reichle, supported by Treasurer Horn, moved to open the 2026 Budget Public Hearing at 7:02 p.m. Carried. The proposed millage rates for the 2026 General Fund, Parks Fund, Capital Projects Fund, Building Inspection Fund, Water Fund, DPW Fund, and Sewer Fund Budgets are to be adopted in compliance with the State of Michigan Public Act 621 of 1978, which amends P.A. 2 of 1968 entitled, The Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act. The two proposed millage rates are as follows: 4.2367 rate generates property tax revenues of $2,936,175 at taxable value of $693,033,589. This rate includes road improvements that were not originally planned for in the previous Budget Hearing. 4.3810 rate generates property tax revenues of $3,036,180 at taxable value of $693,033,589. This rate includes road improvements and $100,000 from the General Fund to help subsidize the substantial water and sewer rate increase. PUBLIC COMMENT – Evelyn Toles from the Park Commission shared information and pricing for park playground equipment to replace the Kid-E-Scape. Members reviewed figures towards this project and asked if the locomotive project funds could be applied to this project. The estimated pricing for this project is near $500,000. Residents asked questions about the water and sewer rates and how this figures into the 2026 Budget. East China Charter Township Official Board Minutes November 10, 2025 Trustee Reichle, supported by Trustee Babel, moved to close the Public Hearing at 7:15 p.m. Carried. PUBLIC COMMENT FOR WATER & SEWER RATES Lori Eschenburg, 4495 Clarke Drive reviewed information regarding the impacts of such a substantial increase in the water and sewer rates and how this will affect already strained, residents’ household expenses. Water consumption has decreased. She asked the Board to consider all financial resources to reduce the impact on our residents. She asked about our Capital Improvement Plan and balance of funds. Supervisor Westrick explained that members of the Board have had multiple water and sewer rate workshops to review all possible funding sources to cover the large debt that was incurred over the past couple years of new water main and sewer main replacements. Many options were considered. He explained that the new rate structure proposal has $25,000 per year for the CIP for water and $75,000 sewer each year + $20,000 sewer equipment replacement. He said that this new infrastructure should have been a voted millage to cover the $9.5 million debt. He also stated that the Township is in good financial condition. A resident said that the hose at the outside spigot at the water plant has many people coming during the night to fill large tanks and trucks. This water is not being paid for, which impacts the costs. Residents asked for more information regarding this whole process. They want to know how we got here and the details; what options are being considered when determining these water and sewer rates. Residents asked why a debt re-payment plan was not put into place for the $9.5 million when this loan was being applied for. Residents asked that oversight be put into place so that this does not happen again; where the residents will be charged such significant increases. Residents asked if there were experts consulted during this process regarding the rate recommendation. Residents asked about selling water to other communities. We have existing emergency Agreements in place for water and piping that connects to St. Clair and Marine City. Residents asked about China Township. East China supplies water to China Township at a cost. China Township is a partner in the water plant and is a member of the Water & Sewer Authority. Trustee Reichle stated that over the last 10-year period, we have paid over $1-million for senior management wages and benefits. He stated that we need to look at all areas in the budget to cut expenses. He suggested that we re-allocate the Capital Improvement Funds set aside for the new DPW building, and the funds for the Township Hall addition. That would add up to about $1million dollars. He said we have more staff in water and sewer than Marine City/St. Clair. Years ago, we had one Superintendent for both Water & Sewer Plants. We were the only one in the East China Charter Township Official Board Minutes November 10, 2025 County to have a Township Manager and Director of Public Services. He said the elected officials are not doing their job. He suggested reducing the wages of the Treasurer, Clerk, & Supervisor until they show what they are doing to fulfill their positions. He said we need to safeguard taxpayer money for the future and demand accountability. He said we are the highest water/sewer rates and taxes in the County. He said we have executive level staff doing elected Officials duties. He said we need to go line by line of each employee and cut what we don’t need. He said the Township Manager position was a failure. He said we have no summer recreation program. He said do away with the pension program for elected Officials. He said to look at different ways of managing staffing levels. Trustee Kline said that he has viewed the Capital Improvement Plan. We need to have funds set aside for the future in case something goes wrong. He agrees to look at all positions and review what is not needed. Then a $500,000 playground is introduced. We need to look at the Budget and see what is not needed. He suggested we subsidize the water and sewer rates this year with $1,000,000 Capital Improvement Funds that were set aside from DPW and Township Hall Buildings. He said next year we will need a new plan. Treasurer Horn said we need to review the next budget line by line at a budget meeting. She recommended not replacing the Director position. She recommended subsidizing the water/sewer rates with existing funds/Fund Balance. Clerk Smith said that all Departments are not overstaffed. The Manager position was created right before the major infrastructure project began, so that person could coordinate the project with the Engineers and Contractors. Trustee Babel asked who would absorb the workload of the Director if not replaced. Trustee Biebuyck said that a lot of work went into reviewing these water/sewer rates by attending workshops. We have a good township. She asked who would do these jobs of Clerk, Treasurer, Supervisor with zero pay. She is not in favor of ripping off the band-aid. She is a retiree also who will have a double digit increase in water/sewer charges. She does not like personal attacks on the Board. She has been the Deputy Clerk now for a year with a lot to learn. She will not argue on this Board between members. She asked to move NB-4 to after NB-1. Trustee Reichle, supported by Trustee Biebuyck, moved to change NB-1 to after NB-4. Carried. Trustee Reichle, supported by Trustee Kline, moved to change NB-2 to after NB-1. Carried. Members proposed that we use General Fund Balance to subsidize the water and sewer rates, adopting the 4.3810 millage rate, and taking the DPW Building and Township Hall addition funds reserve and using these funds to reduce the ready to serve charge. East China Charter Township Official Board Minutes November 10, 2025 NEW BUSINESS NB 3 - CLOSED SESSION FOR UNION CONTRACT NEGOTIATIONS Treasurer Horn, supported by Trustee Babel, moved to close the regular meeting and enter into Closed Session at 9:00 p.m. Carried. Trustee Reichle, supported by Trustee Kline, moved to open the regular meeting at 8:38 p.m. Carried. NB 4 – Director of Public Service Transition Plan Supervisor Westrick proposed that we not replace the Director position, and promote Bookkeeper Garwood to Township Office Supervisor. She would then move from the Clerical IUOE 324 unit to the Supervisor IUOE Unit. This would maintain continuity within our organizational structure. All four Department Supervisor’s would report to the Township Supervisor. He is looking into contracting with our Township Planner from Wade-Trim for one day per week inhouse for grant writing purposes and project planning. Clerk Smith, supported by Treasurer Horn, moved to postpone action of promoting the Bookkeeper to Office Supervisor, until the next meeting November 17, 2025. Carried. NB 1 – Resolution 14-2025 Adopt the 2026 Budgets at 4.3810 Millage Rate RESOLUTION 14-2025 ADOPT 2026 BUDGETS FOR THE GENERAL FUND, PARKS FUND, CAPITAL PROJECTS FUND, BUILDING INSPECTION, WATER, SEWER & DPW FUNDS East China Charter Township County of St. Clair, Michigan Minutes of a regular meeting of the Township Board of Trustees of East China Township, County of St. Clair, Michigan, held in the Township Hall, on the 10TH day of November 2025 at 7:00 p.m. PRESENT: Westrick, Smith, Horn, Babel, Biebuyck, Reichle, Kline. ABSENT: None. The following Resolution was offered by Westrick and supported by Smith. WHEREAS, under the provisions of the Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act 621 of 1978 for local units of government in Michigan, all budgets for the General Fund, Capital Projects Fund, and Debt Service Funds must be adopted by the Legislative Body, which is the East China Charter Township Board of Trustees, and East China Charter Township Official Board Minutes November 10, 2025 WHEREAS, the East China Charter Township Supervisor has submitted proposed 2026 Budgets for the General Fund, Parks Fund, Capital Projects Fund, Building Inspection Fund, Water Fund, DPW Fund and Sewer Fund using a cost center approach in accordance with the Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act, P.A. 621 of 1978, and WHEREAS, pursuant to MCL 42.26, notice of a public hearing on the proposed budget was published in the Times Herald newspaper of general circulation on November 3, 2025, and a Public Hearing on the proposed budgets was held in the East China Charter Township Hall at 7:00 p.m. on November 10, 2025, and WHEREAS, estimated township general fund revenues for fiscal year 2026, including an allocated millage of: 4.3810 generates property tax revenues of $3,036,180 at taxable value of $ 693,033,589 WHEREAS, the East China Charter Township Board of Trustees is authorized to levy and collect general property taxes on all real and personal, property within the township upon the current tax rolls up to 5.0 mills for General Operations and up to the amounts necessary to service bonds voted by the electorate, NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the above recommended 2026 General Fund, Parks Fund, Capital Projects Fund, Building Inspection Fund, Water Fund, DPW Fund, and Sewer Fund Budgets be adopted in compliance with the State of Michigan Public Act 621 of 1978, which amends P. A. 2 of 1968 entitled, "The Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act," and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the East China Charter Township levies the following millage for the 2026 fiscal year: East China Township Operating 4.3810 All resolutions and parts of resolutions insofar as they conflict with the provisions of this Resolution be and the same hereby are rescinded. AYES: Westrick, Smith, Horn, Kline, Babel, Biebuyck. NAYS: Reichle. ABSENT: None. RESOLUTION DECLARED ADOPTED. NB 2 – Water and Sewer Rate Increase East China Charter Township Official Board Minutes November 10, 2025 Trustee Reichle, supported by Treasurer Horn, moved to postpone the water and sewer rate increase to the next meeting on November 17, 2025. Carried. This will require $1.2 Million dollars from the General Fund Balance to subsidize these rates effective January 1, 2026. The proposed revised rate structure is as follows: • • Ready to Serve water $39.29 (20%)/Rate per 1,000 gallons $9.88 (13.4%) Ready to Serve sewer $44.92 (20%)/Rate per 1,000 gallons $7.01 (20%) ADJOURN – Trustee Reichle, supported by Clerk Smith, moved to adjourn at 9:50 p.m. Carried. Sandra Smith, Clerk Verne Westrick, Supervisor

Public Hearings. All public hearings must be held as part of a regular or special meeting of the Zoning Board of Appeals. The following rules of procedure shall apply to public hearings held by the Zoning Board of Appeals: 1. Chairperson opens the public hearing and announces the subject. 2. Chairperson summarizes the procedures/rules to be followed during the hearing. 3. Township staff summarizes the application. 4. Applicant presents the main points of the application. 5. Persons having comments on the application are recognized. 6. Chairperson closes the public hearing and returns to the regular/special meeting. 7. Township consultants (if any) present their report and recommendation. 8. Zoning Board members begin deliberations and arrive at a decision. To ensure everyone has the opportunity to speak, the Chairperson may elect to limit the time permitted for each person to speak, except that the applicant may be permitted additional time as the Chairperson allows. The Chairperson may also elect to allow persons to speak only once, until all persons have had the opportunity to speak, at which time the Chairperson, in his/her discretion, may permit additional comments. All comments by the public, staff, and the Zoning Board shall be directed to the Chairperson. All comments shall be related to the request; unrelated comments shall be ruled out of order. A written notice containing the decision of the Zoning Board of Appeals will be sent to petitioners and originators of the request. Public Hearing: Bachman Trust, PZBA2026-02, Parcel #s: 4706-24-100-013, 4706-24-100-011 Article VI SFR – Single Family Residential, Section 6.06 – Dimensional Requirements Except as Otherwise Specified in this Ordinance: Variance request to create a parcel with less than 120 feet of lot width / road frontage Chairman Frenger opened the public hearing and read the instructions. Dan Davenport 6870 Grand River, Brighton, Michigan 48814 for the Bachman Trust requested that the property be split into 8 parcels. The parent parcel was purchased in 1956. Proposed parcel #1 has road access at the intersection of Monterey Court and Edgemont Drive. The existing width (54.27 feet) of Public Road frontage can support a driveway for a single-family residence. Driveway Site distance has been approved by Livingston County Road Commission. The 66 feet width of the parcel is not the width of the public road frontage. The split into individual parcels still requires review and approval by the Township Planning Commissioners. Call to the Public: David Dean Wade 800 East Allen Road – Email No Objection Howell Township ZBA Meeting Minutes 10/20/2026 Draft Davita J. Finley 2467 Fisher Road -Handwritten note on Notice of Public Hearing letter in opposition to the request Staff Report Finding of Facts The Ordinance currently requires the following: • Section 26.02-C: The required minimum area and road frontage for each lot, parcel, or site area shall be equal to the minimum lot or parcel width as required in each zoning district. • As shown in the zoning map, these parcels are in the Single- F a m i l y Residential • Zoning District. Section 6.06-C: Minimum of 120 feet for a one (1) acre or more parcel and a minimum of 70 feet for 10,000 square feet to less than (1) acre parcel. As proposed, parcel 1 is a 13.19-acre parcel with 1.75 acres of upland area and would have, according to the survey, 54.27 feet of road frontage, meeting neither the 120-foot nor the 70-foot requirement for Single Family Residential parcels: The Township has historically read the deﬁnition of Building Setback Line to mean that a structure cannot be built on a parcel unless it is sited on the property outside of the parcel setbacks and meets the building setback line standard of the Zoning Ordinance. It is common for parcels in the Township to not have the required road frontage required in the Ordinance. An example of this is a parcel that does not have road frontage, but has an easement for ingress and egress, which is usually at most 66 feet wide, but is usually less. Another nearby example is a parcel that is a ﬂag Howell Township ZBA Meeting Minutes 10/20/2026 Draft lot, which has a tail of property connecting the larger portion of the parcel to Fisher Road that is approximately 20 feet wide for their driveway, but which structure meets the property setbacks and the building setback line requirements. While the applicant also raises the deﬁnition of Lot, Waterfront in defense of the request, this deﬁnition does not apply to this request due to the deﬁnitions of Lot, and Lot of Record, because Parcel 1 does not yet exist and is therefore not a Lot of Record. Deﬁnitions: • Building Setback Line: The line formed by the outer surface of a structure or enclosure wall at or with the ﬁnish grade or surface of the ground; pertaining to and deﬁning those minimum (building) setback lines which are established, in general, parallel to the front road right-of-way line and within which setback area no part of a building shall project or be located, except as otherwise provided for by this Ordinance. • Building Line: A line formed by the face of the building, and for the purposes of this Ordinance, a minimum building line is the same as the front setback line. • Lot: A portion of land divided in conformance with all of the provisions of Public Act 288 of 1967 in accordance with Public Act 288 Land Division Act of 1967 as amended, Subdivision Control Act and the Subdivision Regulations of Howell Township. • Lot of Record: A lot existing prior to the adoption of this Ordinance and recorded in the office of the County Register of Deeds. For the purposes of this Ordinance, land contracts and purchase options not recorded in the County Register of Deeds’ Office but dated and executed prior to the effective date of the Ordinance shall also constitute a “lot of record”. (Includes “Parcel of Record”) • Lot, Waterfront: A lot having a frontage directly upon a lake, river or other reasonably sized impoundment of water. The portion adjacent to the water shall be designated as the lake frontage of the lot, and the opposite side shall be designated the road frontage of the lot. • Road Frontage: The legal line of demarcation between a dedicated road right-of-way or easement and abutting land. • Road Line: The line which forms the outer limits of a road right-of-way or easement, and which forms the line from which all road setbacks and front yards are measured. Zoning Ordinance Standards For the ZBA to approve a dimensional variance the applicant must demonstrate a practical difficulty. The ZBA should review the documents submitted by the applicant supporting the variance request against the provisions of the Ordinance, Section 22.07: 1. That special conditions and circumstances exist which are peculiar to the land use, land, structure or building in the same zoning district. • Parcel 4706-24-100-013 is an odd shape, including a road stub off Edgemont Drive. It appears that a much larger development was anticipated that would extend Edgemont Drive through the existing parcel to Pineway Trail allowing for more parcels and more homes to be built. The proposed lot is also an odd shape. While the proposed parcel may not meet the strict letter of the Ordinance, it meets the Howell Township ZBA Meeting Minutes 10/20/2026 Draft spirit of the Ordinance by providing access to a public road no less than 20 feet in width, as required by Section 26.03 and 26.13. 2. That literal interpretation of the provisions of this Ordinance would deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties in the same zoning district under the provisions of this Ordinance. • As stated above, there are a lot of parcels in the Township that have no road frontage, only an easement, or have less than the building setback line frontage as road frontage but still have the required access to a public road. 3. That granting of the variance requested will not confer on the applicant any special privilege that is denied by the provisions of this Ordinance to other lands, structures, or buildings in the same zoning district. • It is common in the Township for property to have less than the building setback line amount of road frontage. 4. That no nonconforming uses of other lands, structures, or buildings in the same zoning district, and not permitted use of lands, structures or buildings in other zoning districts, shall be considered grounds for the issuance of a variance. 5. Applicants shall also follow the outline of requirements prescribed by the Zoning Board of Appeals when applying for an appeal for an interpretation of or a variance from the provisions or requirements of this Zoning Ordinance. 6. Reasons set forth in the application justify the granting of the variance, and the variance is the minimum variance that will make possible the reasonable use of the land, building, or structure in the zoning district in which it is located. • The road stub from Edgemont Drive already exists and is over 20’ wide which is enough for access for a single driveway making the request larger than the minimum. 7. The granting of the variance will be in harmony with the general purpose and intent of this Ordinance, and will not be injurious or otherwise detrimental to the public welfare of the zoning district in which it is to be located. • One additional residential driveway on Edgemont Drive will be in harmony with the Ordinance and will not be detrimental to any existing property or owners in this residential area. Respectfully submitted, Jonathan Hohenstein Howell Township Zoning Administrator Motion by Counts, Second by Weaver, “I move that the Zoning Board of Appeals approve the request of Dan Davenport, on behalf of the Bachman Trust, for a dimensional variance from Sections 6.06(C) and 26.02(C) of the Zoning Ordinance to permit proposed Parcel 1, to be split from Parcel No. 4706-24-100-013, to have 54.27 feet of road frontage where 120 feet is required in the ordinance, with access to Edgemont Drive provided by an exclusive private driveway easement, based on the application materials, the Zoning Administrator’s staff report, and the testimony and evidence presented at the hearing, for the following reasons: The Applicant has demonstrated a practical difficulty because, due to the irregular shape of the parent parcel and proposed Parcel 1, including the existing road stub off Edgemont Drive, the width Howell Township ZBA Meeting Minutes 10/20/2026 Draft of proposed Parcel 1 is not located along its public road frontage, making strict compliance with the road frontage requirement of Section 26.02(C) unnecessarily burdensome. In compliance with Section 22.07(A), the applicant has shown that there are special conditions and circumstances associated with the irregular shape of the parent parcel and proposed Parcel 1, including the existing road stub off Edgemont Drive, within the Single-Family Residential District that make it difficult to comply with Section 26.02 of the Zoning Ordinance. In compliance with Section 22.07(A)(2), applicant has shown that the literal interpretation of the ordinance would deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties in the Single Family Residential District because there are other parcels within this district that have no road frontage, only an easement, or have less than the building setback line frontage as road frontage but still have required public road access, example Flagpole Lots. In compliance with Section 22.07(A)(3), the applicant has shown that the granting of the variance will not confer any special privilege that is denied to others within the same zoning district because it is common for properties within the Single-Family Residential to have less than the building setback line amount of road frontage. In compliance with Section 22.07(A)(4), no nonconforming uses of other lands, structures, or buildings in the district, and no permitted uses of lands, structures, or buildings in other zoning districts, have been considered as grounds for the issuance of this variance. In compliance with Section 22.07(B), applicant has followed the outline of requirements prescribed by the Zoning Board of Appeals in applying for this variance. In compliance with Section 22.07(C), subject to the conditions set forth below, the variance is the minimum variance that will make possible the reasonable use of the land in the SFR District because the variance is limited to proposed Parcel 1 and the exclusive driveway easement will be limited in width, which provides access to a public road consistent with Sections 26.03 and 26.13. In compliance with Section 22.07(D), the granting of the variance will be in harmony with the general purpose and intent of the Zoning Ordinance and will not be injurious or otherwise detrimental to the public welfare within the Single Family Residential District because one additional residential driveway on Edgemont Drive has minimal to no impact on the surrounding properties, including the adjoining parcels currently owned by the applicant, and the Livingston County Road Commission has recommended approval.” Roll Call: McEvoy- yes, Weaver- yes, Countsyes, Frenger- yes, Williams- yes. It would be subject to the maximum square footage allowed of 3,000 square feet of accessory structures or 4% of lot area. Historically the Township has used the more restrictive regulation. There are currently four small accessory structures that total approximately 337 square feet and a detached garage that is 1,472 square feet for a total of 1,809 square feet of current accessory structures. Jason’s drawings indicate that the proposed accessory structure is 80’ x 40’ or 3,200 square feet. Launched by Michigan Audubon in 2025, with founding partner Ford Motor Company, Bird City Michigan is a science-based program that recognizes communities for taking meaningful action to protect birds and their habitats. The program is part of the international Bird City Network and encourages municipalities, conservation organizations, and residents to work together to create healthier environments for both birds and people. “We are beyond proud to earn this designation through our current stewardship efforts, which take place all year round with dedicated staff and volunteers. Reducing bird-window collisions at Township buildings and continuing to restore native plant populations is our main goal to help local birds thrive,” said Land Stewardship Coordinator Emma Campbell. Meridian Township earned the designation through its ongoing efforts to preserve natural areas, enhance wildlife habitat, promote environmental stewardship, and engage the community in conservation initiatives. The Township's application highlighted local programs and partnerships that support habitat protection, environmental education, and sustainable land management. “Michigan Audubon is especially proud to welcome the Township as a Bird City Michigan community. While our reach is statewide, our headquarters are located right here in Meridian Township. The collaboration among the Township's staff and volunteers exemplifies a community creating spaces where both wildlife and people can thrive,” said Linda Smith, Director of Partnerships for Michigan Audubon. Michigan Audubon connects birds and people for the benefit of both through conservation, education, and research across Michigan. Incorporated in 1905, the organization stewards more than 4,000 acres of habitat at 20 bird sanctuaries throughout the state. For more information, contact Michigan Audubon at birdcity@michiganaudubon.org. The Bird City Michigan-Meridian Township team included Township staff, the Meridian Green Team, the Meridian Township Environmental Commission, the Harris Nature Center, the Meridian Conservation Corps (MCC), and the Capital Area Audubon Society. Together, the team completed the application process and identified opportunities to further support bird conservation efforts within the community. -more- The community of Meridian Township is in close proximity to the Michigan State Capitol and Michigan State University. The Township serves the community through exceptional services, beneficial amenities and an outstanding quality of life. It is a welcoming community that celebrates quality education, recreation and lifestyles. Zoning Ordinance Text Amendments to: • Update Article 2, Section 2.2, of the Township of Oxford Zoning Ordinance, to establish a definition of “Data Center” and provide regulations for large-scale data processing, computer server, data storage, telecommunications equipment, cryptocurrency data mining, and associated infrastructure uses. These facilities are used for the processing, storage, and transmission of digital information and may include supporting infrastructure such as backup power generation, cooling systems, fuel storage, and security systems. • Update Article 10, Section 10.1.H., 10.1.J and 10.1.K, to modify electromagnetic interference, noise and vibration standards for all uses in the Township. These standards will be applicable to data centers as well as all other uses in the Township. • Update Article 3, Section 3.5, to make data centers a special land use in the Data Center Overlay District (DCO). This overlay has been applied to Light Industrial (I-1) and General Industrial (I-2) zoned parcels north of Hummer Lake Road and south of Xcelsior Drive, and between Xcelsior Drive and M-24. The Data Center Overlay (DCO) is an overlay designation and does not replace the underlying zoning district. Data centers may be considered as special land uses only on property within the DCO that is also zoning I-1 or I-2, subject to Section 5.41. • Add a new section to Article 5, Section 5.41. This section addresses required noise studies, cooling system design, anticipated utility demand and capacity verification, traffic analysis, screening and sound barrier standards, security measures, backup power generation and fuel storage, decommissioning plans, development agreements, impact assessments, public service training and equipment requirements, setbacks, renewable energy requirements, thermal emission standards, annual reports requirements, architectural standards, and performance violations and remedies. • Update Article 4, Section 4.7, to clarify the process under which a special land use permit may be suspended or revoked by the Township Board of Trustees for all special land uses in the Township. • Add Appendix A to the zoning ordinance. The appendix is titled “Oxford Township Data Center Engineering Requirements” and provides required information, designs, and standards relating to municipal water supply and sewer, water supply for cooling, water recycling, water discharge, hydrology, stormwater management, traffic and site access, ground wells, environmental impact assessments, and construction planning as it relates to data centers. • Add Appendix B to the zoning ordinance. The appendix is titled “Oxford Township Fire Department Data Center Fire and Life Safety Review Requirements” and provides required information, designs, and standards relating to fire protection systems, water supply, battery energy storage systems, backup power generation and fuel storage, emergency access and site operations, pre-incident planning, and emergency coordination as it relates to data centers.
